div.div: سَلَمَان or سَلِمَان, accord. to different readings, occurs in a trad. of Ibn-'Omar, in which it is said, كَانَ يُصَلِّى عِنْدَ سَلَمَانٍ فِى طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ [He used to pray at certain selem-trees, or certain stones, in the road of Mekkeh]: each may be a pl. [or rather a quasi-pl. n.]; the former, of ↓ سَلَمَةٌ , the “ tree so called; ” the latter, of ↓ سَلِمَةٌ , “ stones ” [or a “ stone: ” but both of these explanations are strange]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
